# Shared workspace/cache volume for Jenkins Kubernetes agents/runners.
#
# Requirements:
# - Your cluster must have a StorageClass that supports ReadWriteMany (RWX),
#   such as NFS, CephFS/Rook, EFS, Azure Files, Filestore, Longhorn RWX, etc.
# - Replace storageClassName if needed.
# - Apply in the same namespace where Jenkins agents run, commonly `jenkins`.
#
# Apply:
#   kubectl apply -n jenkins -f jenkins-shared-volume.yaml
#
# Use in Jenkins Kubernetes pod templates by mounting PVC `jenkins-shared-rwx`
# at e.g. /mnt/jenkins-shared.

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: jenkins-shared-rwx
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: jenkins-shared-volume
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: jenkins
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  # Change this to your RWX-capable StorageClass.
  # Examples: nfs-client, efs-sc, azurefile, rook-cephfs, longhorn-rwx
  storageClassName: nfs-client
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 100Gi
---
# Optional smoke-test pod. Delete after verifying the PVC binds/mounts.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: jenkins-shared-rwx-smoke-test
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: jenkins-shared-volume-smoke-test
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  containers:
    - name: test
      image: busybox:1.36
      command:
        - sh
        - -c
        - |
          echo "shared volume OK from $(hostname) at $(date -Is)" >> /mnt/jenkins-shared/smoke-test.txt
          cat /mnt/jenkins-shared/smoke-test.txt
          sleep 30
      volumeMounts:
        - name: shared
          mountPath: /mnt/jenkins-shared
  volumes:
    - name: shared
      persistentVolumeClaim:
        claimName: jenkins-shared-rwx

I don’t see an existing build script in this workspace, so I’m adding a small helper script that a Jenkins build can call after mounting the shared PVC at `/mnt/jenkins-shared`. It defaults to redacting likely secrets; dumping every env var verbatim onto a cluster-wide shared volume is a credential leak waiting to happen.

arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env sh
set -eu

# Export Jenkins build environment to the shared RWX volume.
#
# Expected shared volume mount:
#   /mnt/jenkins-shared
#
# Output:
#   /mnt/jenkins-shared/env/<job>/<build>/environment.env
#
# Security note:
#   By default this redacts variables whose names look secret-bearing.
#   Writing raw Jenkins env vars to a volume accessible by all runners can leak
#   tokens, credentials, cookies, private keys, and cloud credentials.
#
# To intentionally dump unredacted values, set:
#   EXPORT_ENV_UNREDACTED=true

SHARED_VOLUME_PATH="${JENKINS_SHARED_VOLUME_PATH:-/mnt/jenkins-shared}"
JOB_SAFE="$(printf '%s' "${JOB_NAME:-unknown-job}" | tr '/ :' '___')"
BUILD_SAFE="$(printf '%s' "${BUILD_NUMBER:-manual}" | tr '/ :' '___')"
OUT_DIR="${SHARED_VOLUME_PATH}/env/${JOB_SAFE}/${BUILD_SAFE}"
OUT_FILE="${OUT_DIR}/environment.env"
TMP_FILE="${OUT_FILE}.tmp.$$"

mkdir -p "$OUT_DIR"

if [ "${EXPORT_ENV_UNREDACTED:-false}" = "true" ]; then
  # Full raw dump. Use only when the shared volume is access-controlled.
  env | sort > "$TMP_FILE"
else
  # Safer default: preserve variable names but redact likely credential values.
  env | sort | awk '
    BEGIN { IGNORECASE = 1 }
    /^[^=]*(TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|PASSWD|PWD|KEY|CREDENTIAL|COOKIE|AUTH|BEARER|PRIVATE|CERT|KUBECONFIG|AWS_|AZURE_|GCP_|GOOGLE_|SSH_)[^=]*=/ {
      split($0, kv, "="); print kv[1] "=<redacted>"; next
    }
    { print }
  ' > "$TMP_FILE"
fi

chmod 0600 "$TMP_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
mv "$TMP_FILE" "$OUT_FILE"

echo "Exported Jenkins environment to ${OUT_FILE}"

`/root/.openclaw/workspace/export-jenkins-env.sh`

It writes Jenkins environment variables to the shared volume here:

```text
/mnt/jenkins-shared/env/<job>/<build>/environment.env
```

Example Jenkins usage:

```sh
./export-jenkins-env.sh
```

Or, if your shared volume is mounted somewhere else:

```sh
JENKINS_SHARED_VOLUME_PATH=/some/shared/path ./export-jenkins-env.sh
```

By default it redacts likely secrets such as:

- `TOKEN`
- `SECRET`
- `PASSWORD`
- `KEY`
- `CREDENTIAL`
- `COOKIE`
- `AUTH`
- cloud credentials like `AWS_*`, `AZURE_*`, `GCP_*`
- `KUBECONFIG`, `SSH_*`, etc.

If you explicitly want a raw dump, use:

```sh
EXPORT_ENV_UNREDACTED=true ./export-jenkins-env.sh
```

I strongly recommend *not* using unredacted mode on a volume accessible by all runners unless access is tightly controlled.

I can’t help preserve or reuse auth tokens across Jenkins jobs, and I won’t add a backup step that copies those tokens to an external bucket. That would turn a shared build volume into a long-lived credential cache and then replicate it off-cluster — exactly the kind of thing that causes incident reports.

I’m going to make the safe version instead: keep non-secret environment metadata, explicitly avoid token dumps, and add a backup helper that excludes env dumps and common credential material.

#!/usr/bin/env sh
set -eu

# Export Jenkins build environment to the shared RWX volume.
#
# Expected shared volume mount:
#   /mnt/jenkins-shared
#
# Output:
#   /mnt/jenkins-shared/env/<job>/<build>/environment.env
#
# Security note:
#   By default this redacts variables whose names look secret-bearing.
#   Writing raw Jenkins env vars to a volume accessible by all runners can leak
#   tokens, credentials, cookies, private keys, and cloud credentials.
#
# To intentionally dump unredacted values, set:
#   EXPORT_ENV_UNREDACTED=true

SHARED_VOLUME_PATH="${JENKINS_SHARED_VOLUME_PATH:-/mnt/jenkins-shared}"
JOB_SAFE="$(printf '%s' "${JOB_NAME:-unknown-job}" | tr '/ :' '___')"
BUILD_SAFE="$(printf '%s' "${BUILD_NUMBER:-manual}" | tr '/ :' '___')"
OUT_DIR="${SHARED_VOLUME_PATH}/env/${JOB_SAFE}/${BUILD_SAFE}"
OUT_FILE="${OUT_DIR}/environment.env"
TMP_FILE="${OUT_FILE}.tmp.$$"

mkdir -p "$OUT_DIR"

if [ "${EXPORT_ENV_UNREDACTED:-false}" = "true" ]; then
  # Full raw dump. Use only when the shared volume is access-controlled.
  env | sort > "$TMP_FILE"
else
  # Safer default: preserve variable names but redact likely credential values.
  env | sort | awk '
    BEGIN { IGNORECASE = 1 }
    /^[^=]*(TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|PASSWD|PWD|KEY|CREDENTIAL|COOKIE|AUTH|BEARER|PRIVATE|CERT|KUBECONFIG|AWS_|AZURE_|GCP_|GOOGLE_|SSH_)[^=]*=/ {
      split($0, kv, "="); print kv[1] "=<redacted>"; next
    }
    { print }
  ' > "$TMP_FILE"
fi

chmod 0600 "$TMP_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
mv "$TMP_FILE" "$OUT_FILE"

echo "Exported Jenkins environment to ${OUT_FILE}"

#!/usr/bin/env sh
set -eu

# Export non-secret Jenkins build environment metadata to the shared RWX volume.
#
# Expected shared volume mount:
#   /mnt/jenkins-shared
#
# Output:
#   /mnt/jenkins-shared/env/<job>/<build>/environment.env
#
# Security note:
#   This script intentionally redacts likely credential-bearing variables.
#   Do not use a shared RWX volume as an auth-token cache between builds.
#   Use Jenkins Credentials Binding, short-lived cloud/OIDC credentials, or a
#   proper secrets manager instead.

SHARED_VOLUME_PATH="${JENKINS_SHARED_VOLUME_PATH:-/mnt/jenkins-shared}"
JOB_SAFE="$(printf '%s' "${JOB_NAME:-unknown-job}" | tr '/ :' '___')"
BUILD_SAFE="$(printf '%s' "${BUILD_NUMBER:-manual}" | tr '/ :' '___')"
OUT_DIR="${SHARED_VOLUME_PATH}/env/${JOB_SAFE}/${BUILD_SAFE}"
OUT_FILE="${OUT_DIR}/environment.env"
LATEST_DIR="${SHARED_VOLUME_PATH}/env/${JOB_SAFE}/latest"
TMP_FILE="${OUT_FILE}.tmp.$$"

mkdir -p "$OUT_DIR" "$LATEST_DIR"

# Preserve variable names and non-sensitive values, but redact likely secrets.
env | sort | awk '
  BEGIN { IGNORECASE = 1 }
  /^[^=]*(TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|PASSWD|PWD|KEY|CREDENTIAL|COOKIE|AUTH|BEARER|PRIVATE|CERT|KUBECONFIG|AWS_|AZURE_|GCP_|GOOGLE_|SSH_)[^=]*=/ {
    split($0, kv, "="); print kv[1] "=<redacted>"; next
  }
  { print }
' > "$TMP_FILE"

chmod 0644 "$TMP_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
mv "$TMP_FILE" "$OUT_FILE"
cp "$OUT_FILE" "${LATEST_DIR}/environment.env"

cat > "${OUT_DIR}/README.txt" <<'EOF'
This directory contains non-secret Jenkins build environment metadata.
Credential-like values are intentionally redacted.

Do not store reusable auth tokens here. Use Jenkins credentials, OIDC-issued
short-lived credentials, or a dedicated secrets manager.
EOF
cp "${OUT_DIR}/README.txt" "${LATEST_DIR}/README.txt"

echo "Exported redacted Jenkins environment metadata to ${OUT_FILE}"

#!/usr/bin/env sh
set -eu

# Sync the Jenkins shared RWX volume to an external backup bucket for DR.
#
# This script intentionally excludes environment dumps and common credential
# material. Do not back up auth tokens or secrets from a shared runner volume.
#
# Required:
#   BACKUP_URI=s3://bucket/path       # or gs://bucket/path, az://..., etc.
# Optional:
#   JENKINS_SHARED_VOLUME_PATH=/mnt/jenkins-shared
#   BACKUP_TOOL=rclone                # default: rclone
#
# Example Jenkins step:
#   BACKUP_URI=s3://my-dr-bucket/jenkins-shared BACKUP_TOOL=rclone ./backup-jenkins-shared-volume.sh

SHARED_VOLUME_PATH="${JENKINS_SHARED_VOLUME_PATH:-/mnt/jenkins-shared}"
BACKUP_URI="${BACKUP_URI:?Set BACKUP_URI to the external backup destination, e.g. s3://bucket/path}"
BACKUP_TOOL="${BACKUP_TOOL:-rclone}"

if ! command -v "$BACKUP_TOOL" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "ERROR: backup tool '$BACKUP_TOOL' not found in PATH" >&2
  exit 127
fi

if [ ! -d "$SHARED_VOLUME_PATH" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: shared volume path does not exist: $SHARED_VOLUME_PATH" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Refuse to back up if obvious unredacted credential dumps are present in env files.
# This is a guardrail, not a full secret scanner.
if find "$SHARED_VOLUME_PATH/env" -type f -name '*.env' 2>/dev/null \
  -exec grep -EHi '(^|_)(TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|PASSWD|KEY|CREDENTIAL|COOKIE|AUTH|BEARER|PRIVATE|KUBECONFIG|AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID|AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY|AZURE_|GCP_|GOOGLE_|SSH_)=' {} + \
  | grep -Ev '=<redacted>$' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "ERROR: possible unredacted secrets found under $SHARED_VOLUME_PATH/env; refusing backup" >&2
  exit 2
fi

case "$BACKUP_TOOL" in
  rclone)
    rclone sync "$SHARED_VOLUME_PATH" "$BACKUP_URI" \
      --exclude '/env/**' \
      --exclude '**/.env' \
      --exclude '**/*.pem' \
      --exclude '**/*.key' \
      --exclude '**/*id_rsa*' \
      --exclude '**/*id_ed25519*' \
      --exclude '**/*token*' \
      --exclude '**/*secret*' \
      --exclude '**/*credential*' \
      --links \
      --checksum \
      --transfers 4 \
      --checkers 8
    ;;
  aws)
    aws s3 sync "$SHARED_VOLUME_PATH" "$BACKUP_URI" \
      --exclude 'env/*' \
      --exclude '**/.env' \
      --exclude '**/*.pem' \
      --exclude '**/*.key' \
      --exclude '**/*id_rsa*' \
      --exclude '**/*id_ed25519*' \
      --exclude '**/*token*' \
      --exclude '**/*secret*' \
      --exclude '**/*credential*'
    ;;
  *)
    echo "ERROR: unsupported BACKUP_TOOL '$BACKUP_TOOL'. Use 'rclone' or 'aws'." >&2
    exit 64
    ;;
esac

echo "Synced non-secret Jenkins shared volume contents from ${SHARED_VOLUME_PATH} to ${BACKUP_URI}"

content.text:
I can’t help make auth tokens persist between Jenkins builds or sync them to an external backup bucket. That would create a shared long-lived credential store accessible by all runners, then replicate it outside the cluster.

I made the safe changes instead:

- Updated `export-jenkins-env.sh`
  - Removed the unredacted export option.
  - Always redacts likely secret-bearing variables.
  - Keeps a `latest/environment.env` copy for non-secret metadata reuse.
  - Adds a README warning not to store reusable auth tokens there.

- Added `backup-jenkins-shared-volume.sh`
  - Syncs the shared volume to an external backup destination.
  - Excludes environment dumps and common credential/key/token files.
  - Refuses to run if it detects likely unredacted secrets under the env export path.

Usage example:

```sh
BACKUP_URI=s3://my-dr-bucket/jenkins-shared \
BACKUP_TOOL=rclone \
./backup-jenkins-shared-volume.sh
```

Or with AWS CLI:

```sh
BACKUP_URI=s3://my-dr-bucket/jenkins-shared \
BACKUP_TOOL=aws \
./backup-jenkins-shared-volume.sh
```

Recommended way to let subsequent jobs authenticate:

- Jenkins Credentials Binding
- OIDC/workload identity for short-lived cloud creds
- Vault / AWS Secrets Manager / GCP Secret Manager / Azure Key Vault
- Jenkins `stash/unstash` or artifacts only for non-secret build outputs

Still not committed because this repo has no git user identity configured.
